speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Minister Edwin Tong and I will be delivering Ministerial Statements on this matter.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Our Statements will address Oral Question Nos 1 to 23 and Written Question Nos 1 and 9 to 13 on today's Order Paper.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh1,2, Mr Leon Perera, Ms Hazel Poa and Mr Alex Yam3,4 have filed Oral and Written Questions scheduled for future Sittings on this matter.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: As today's Ministerial Statements will address those questions as well, I invite these Members to seek clarifications, should they have any, on this matter after our Ministerial Statements.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: And should their queries be sufficiently addressed, it may not be necessary for them to proceed with their Parliamentary Questions for future Sittings.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Ministers Shanmugam and Balakrishnan had also spoken to Prime Minister Lee to ask for a review that is independent of the Ministries and agencies that they oversee.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Members would have had the opportunity to read and scrutinise the two reports.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: I will now summarise the findings of my Review, which, I should emphasise, relies on CPIB's findings and report, before addressing questions on specific matters which Members had filed.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: First, to establish the facts surrounding the renting out of the two properties at 26 and 31 Ridout Road.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Second, to establish if there was any wrongdoing, including any abuse of power or conflict of interest, resulting in the Ministers gaining an unfair advantage or privileges.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Third, to establish whether the policies and processes governing the renting out of black and white bungalows were followed in renting out the two properties and if there were any process gaps or lapses.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Hence, CPIB's investigation findings would be independent, thorough and authoritative.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: In its investigations, the CPIB conducted interviews with the two Ministers and their spouses, former and current officers from the Ministry of Law (MinLaw), SLA and National Parks Board (NParks), property and managing agents who had knowledge of the rental transactions of the two state properties.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: CPIB also obtained evidence from documents and other information related to the rental transactions and parties involved, including through contemporaneous phone records, WhatsApp messages and SMSes.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: The agency reports directly to him, the Prime Minister – not to the Minister for Home Affairs, nor to me, for that matter, the Coordinating Minister for National Security.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Moreover, the Director of CPIB can go directly to the President if the Prime Minister stops him from investigating a possible crime.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: The Constitution provides the Director of CPIB that right.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: There is no more thorough, persistent and, I dare say, even fearsome investigative body in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: That the Prime Minister did not hesitate to call the CPIB in to investigate two senior Ministers is a signal how seriously we take such matters; incorruptibility is an absolute value in our system.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: In addition to CPIB's investigation, I asked MinLaw to provide a detailed briefing on the policies and processes governing the management of black and white bungalows.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: My review, therefore, relied on CPIB's investigation findings on the renting out of the two properties, and a review of the policies and processes governing the management of black and white bungalows, to come to its conclusions.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Several Members, Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim, Mr Murali Pillai and Mr Pritam Singh, asked about the rental process.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: The 26 Ridout Road state property had a land size of 9,350 square metres then.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Similarly, my Report, which was submitted by the Prime Minister to Parliament, quotes liberally, verbatim from the CPIB report, and Members would have seen those sections in italics.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: I cannot speak in italics, but I will tell Members which part of my Statement I am quoting directly from CPIB.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: So, let me quote directly from CPIB for the next four or five paragraphs. "In January 2018, Minister Shanmugam appointed a property agent to represent him for the rental transaction of the 26 Ridout Road state property.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: By then, the property had been vacant without attracting any bids for more than four years.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: During a site visit, Minister Shanmugam noticed thick and overgrown vegetation on an empty slope of land adjacent to the property.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Minister Shanmugam expressed his concern to SLA that the overgrown vegetation might pose public health and safety risks from snakes, mosquitoes and fallen trees.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Through his property agent, Minister Shanmugam negotiated with SLA on clearing of the adjacent land before leasing the property.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: He was not confident that the adjacent land would be maintained in a way that would keep the place free of health and safety issues.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: He offered to maintain the adjacent land at his own cost.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Minister Shanmugam stated in his interview with CPIB that he had not wanted to lease the additional adjacent land as there would be legal obligations attached to leasing it.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: SLA's view was that the tenant's responsibility would not extend to maintain the area beyond the tenant's property boundary.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: If Minister Shanmugam was to maintain the adjacent land at his own cost, the adjacent land had to be included in the tenancy of the 26 Ridout Road state property.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: SLA then did the fencing of the adjacent land within the property boundary.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: The cost of site clearance, replanting of greenery and fencing was $172,000 which was initially borne by SLA and subsequently to be recovered from the tenant's rent.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: The cost of maintaining this additional land was approximately $25,000 per year and it was incurred by Minister Shanmugam which would otherwise have been borne by SLA.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Minister Shanmugam and his agent were not aware of the guide rent.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: His agent studied the rental of comparable neighbouring properties and independently determined and valued the rent.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Minister Shanmugam instructed his property agent that he should not be paying less than his neighbours.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: As the property had not been in use since 2013, substantial repairs were needed.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: The total cost of essential repair works borne by SLA to restore 26 Ridout Road state property was $515,400.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: The landlord, that is, SLA, has the responsibility to undertake essential repair works to ensure that the condition of the property is habitable.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Minister Shanmugam paid $61,400 to build the car porch.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: In addition, he stated in his interview with CPIB that he paid over $400,000 for additional improvement works to the state property not covered by SLA's restoration works.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Mrs Shanmugam signed the Tenancy Agreement of 3+3+3 years in June 2018.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: After the first three-year term, the tenancy was renewed in June 2021 for a second three-year term.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: For the rental of 31 Ridout Road, the key facts are as follows.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Again, the next three paragraphs are verbatim from the CPIB report. "The No. 31 Ridout Road state property, of land size 9,157.36 square metres, had been vacant since July 2013.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: It was listed on the State Property Information Online website.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: The property had been vacant for five years before two unsuccessful bids were made below the then prevailing guide rent, that is, $12,000 in July 2018 and $5,000 in August 2018.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Mrs Balakrishnan came across a 'For Lease' sign at the No. 31 Ridout Road state property.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: She contacted the SLA's appointed managing agent (MA) on 11 September 2018 and they negotiated on the rental price.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: The MA named an asking rent of $19,000.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Mrs Balakrishnan offered $19,000 with the inclusion of essential repair works and upgrading of the toilet.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: The MA rejected the toilet upgrading as it was considered to be improvement works, and Mrs Balakrishnan subsequently agreed to bear the costs of the toilet upgrading.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: The asking rent for the No. 31 Ridout Road state property was independently determined and valued by the MA.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Neither Minister Balakrishnan nor Mrs Balakrishnan were aware of the guide rent.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: The SLA Leasing Department subsequently accepted the lease proposal, because the final secured rent of $19,000 was not below the prevailing guide rent, which was $18,800.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: The total cost of essential repair works borne by SLA to restore the No. 31 Ridout Road state property was $570,500.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Minister Balakrishnan stated in his interview with CPIB that he paid more than $200,000 on additional improvement works to the state property.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: The tenancy agreement for 3+2+2 years was signed by Mrs Balakrishnan in October 2019.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: After the first three-year term, Mrs Balakrishnan requested and was granted a renewal of another 3+2 year-term instead of 2+2 year-term that was earlier granted.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: The rental for the second term was increased from $19,000 to $20,000 per month, taking into consideration the then-prevailing market conditions in 2022." Unquote.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Again, I must emphasise that the preceding paragraphs were from CPIB's investigation report and findings.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: I will address questions on the rental transactions of these two properties, while Minister Edwin Tong will address questions regarding SLA's policies and practices in the management of state properties in general.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin asked whether the two Ministers' tenancies at Ridout Road from SLA have been handled without any corrupt behaviours.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: In CPIB's view, the Direct Tenancy rules were applied fairly for both rental transactions.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: The investigation did not reveal any corrupt intent on the part of any person or any inducement given to any individual involved in the processing of the rentals.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: CPIB found no preferential treatment given to the Ministers and their spouses and no disclosure of privileged information in the process of the rental transactions.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: There was no evidence to suggest any abuse of position by the Ministers for personal gain." CPIB has submitted its investigation papers to the Attorney-General's Chambers (AGC).

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Mr Dennis Tan, Mr Murali Pillai, Mr Louis Chua, Mr Alex Yam and Ms Hazel Poa asked whether there was any conflict of interest involved in the renting of the two properties to Ministers Shanmugam and Balakrishnan, and if the Ministers had complied with the Code of Conduct for Ministers.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Both the Ministers and the public officers involved duly declared any potential conflict of interest and followed the proper processes to prevent any actual conflict of interest from arising.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: In the case of 26 Ridout Road, as Minister Shanmugam is the Minister for Law, and the Ministry of Law oversees SLA, a conflict of interest could have arisen if Minister Shanmugam had remained in the chain of command exercising authority over the renting out of the property.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: And had Minister Shanmugam made decisions that affected his own rental of 26 Ridout Road, that would have been an actual conflict of interest.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: So, it could have been a conflict of interest.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: If he had taken any decisions affecting his own rental, that would have been an actual conflict of interest.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: However, Minister Shanmugam had removed himself from the chain of command and decision-making process entirely.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: CPIB established that Minister Shanmugam informed the then-Deputy Secretary of the Ministry of Law that he would recuse himself on any discussion related to the rental of the property.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Minister Shanmugam also instructed the then-Deputy Secretary to approach the then-Senior Minister of State in the Ministry of Law, Ms Indranee Rajah, in the event that any matter had to be referred to the Minister.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Minister Shanmugam had also informed me that if the matter had to go beyond Senior Minister of State Indranee Rajah, she would approach me.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: CPIB established that there was no matter raised by SLA to the Ministry of Law and, hence, to any of the Ministers during the entire rental process.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Minister Shanmugam had recognised the potential conflict of interest, duly declared it to me and took effective steps to eliminate this potential conflict.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: CPIB found that due diligence checks were also carried out before the signing of the tenancy agreement for the 26 Ridout Road state property.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: The then-Chief Executive of SLA made a declaration dated 29 March 2018 to the then-Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Law and reported that the processing of the rental transaction was properly done with no conflict of interest.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: In response to the Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Law's queries, the Chief Executive of SLA assured him that the proposed rental was according to market rate with assessment done by SLA valuers, independently of the SLA leasing officers.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: He also confirmed that the tenancy agreement was a standard form for all other residential tenancies.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: In the case of 31 Ridout Road, no issue of conflict of interest arose because Minister Balakrishnan's official responsibilities did not include SLA.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Ms Hazel Poa asked what are the current rules and processes for Cabinet Ministers to declare conflicts of interest and whether there are any plans to strengthen such rules and processes.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Ministers and other political officeholders are notified of this Code at the start of each term of office and whenever a new political officeholder is appointed.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: The Prime Minister also issues Rules of Prudence after every election to all Members of Parliament of the People's Action Party (PAP).

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: These Rules are released to the media, with the latest version released in August 2020.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: The Code clearly states that a Minister must not direct or request a civil servant to do anything or perform any function that may conflict with the Civil Service's core values of incorruptibility, impartiality, integrity and honesty.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Ministers are expected to be scrupulously above board and to ensure that there is no real or perceived conflict between their official duties and private interests.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: The Code and Rules set out the principles to be applied.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: The Code of Conduct and the Rules of Prudence also give examples to illustrate the application of the guidelines, but these examples are not exhaustive.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: The examples are not exhaustive as it is not possible to lay out specific rules governing behaviour for every single situation.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: For the Public Service, the Code of Conduct is set out in the Instruction Manual (IM).

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: All public officers must take an annual Code of Conduct quiz and make the necessary declarations, such as being free of financial embarrassment, their investments in non-owner-occupied properties and their investments in private firms.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: They are also required to make ad hoc declarations of purchases of private residential properties, commercial properties and land.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: The principles laid out in the Codes of Conduct adequately cover any potential conflict of interest that could have arisen, including in this case.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: They were aware of their duty to declare and avoid any conflict of interest, and they took appropriate steps to prevent any potential or actual conflict of interest from arising.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Nevertheless, the Public Service will reference this case as an additional example to reinforce the importance for public officers to act with integrity.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: The officer will have to declare that he has taken adequate steps to prevent any conflict of interest from arising, for example, by recusing himself from overseeing or processing the transaction.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: These properties will include commercial and residential state properties, such as black and white bungalows, terraces, factory/office spaces, business parks, shops in neighbourhood centres, hawker and market stalls.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: The Prime Minister will also review the declarations required for property transactions for Ministers and PAP Members of Parliament.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Mr Murali Pillai, Mr Pritam Singh and Mr Sitoh Yih Pin asked whether the Ministers had benefited from privileged information or from favourable rental rates.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: CPIB found no preferential treatment given to the Ministers or to their spouses and no disclosure of privileged information in the process of the rental transactions.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: There was no evidence to suggest any abuse of position by the Ministers for personal gain.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: CPIB established that the availability of 26 and 31 Ridout Road for lease was public information.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: Both properties had "For Lease" signs displayed prominently at the gates of these properties and, in addition, 31 was listed on the State Property Information Online (SPIO) website.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: The guide rents were not revealed to Minister Shanmugam and his agent, nor to Minister and Mrs Balakrishnan.

speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
text: There was no evidence that the Ministers were given favourable rental rates due to their positions.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: Members may also access the handouts through the MP@SGPARL app.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: These show the rental rates for transactions involving black and white bungalows in the Ridout Road estate at the material time in 2018 and 2019.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: So, these were new transactions at the material times in 2018 and 2019.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: This was comparable to that for the other Ridout Road properties, which ranged from $26.00 per square metre per month to $33.33 per square metre per month.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: However, this was due to the condition of the property.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: The rental of $23.05 per square metre was comparable to other properties of "average" condition at that time.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: When the tenancies of the two properties were up for renewal after the initial three years, a revaluation was done to peg the rentals to the prevailing market rate, that is, to mark them to market.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: This valuation was also based on market comparables.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: The property at 26 Ridout Road was renewed in June 2021 for three years with the rent maintained at $26,500 per month.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: The property at 31 Ridout Road was renewed in October 2022 for three years with the rent increased to $20,000 per month, from $19,000 per month.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: However, CPIB discovered that there was a lack of precision in SLA's use of the term "guide rent" for 26 Ridout Road.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: As a result of this lack of precision, the earlier SLA statement dated 12 May 2023 that the offer by the tenant – that is, $26,500 – was above the guide rent was incorrect.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: The guide rent of 26 Ridout Road, with the original land area of 9,350 square metres, was established by the SLA's Valuer as $24,500.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: From February 2018, SLA and Minister Shanmugam, through his appointed agent, negotiated the rental of 26 Ridout Road.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: Both sides discussed the clearance of the heavily vegetated adjacent land which posed potential public health and safety concerns.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: Minister Shanmugam offered to maintain the adjacent land at his own cost if SLA cleared the vegetation.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: He told CPIB that he preferred to exclude the land from his tenancy, as there would be legal obligations attached to including the adjacent land.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: However, SLA's preference was to include the adjacent land within the property boundary.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: That would make it clear that responsibility for maintaining the land would fall on the tenant, as would the legal obligations, for example, the tenant would be responsible for any mosquito breeding.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: SLA negotiated an agreement with the prospective tenant in which the adjacent land would be included within the property boundary, with the tenant responsible for maintaining it.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: This would make the responsibilities clear and the tenant, rather than SLA, would bear the obligations and the cost of maintaining the land.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: Minister Shanmugam initially offered a rental of $25,000 per month, based on the agent's advice.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: He instructed his property agent that he should not be paying less than his neighbours.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: SLA proposed a rental of $26,500 and this was agreed to by Minister Shanmugam.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: SLA wanted to recover from the tenant the cost of land clearance and new fencing to amalgamate the cleared land.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: SLA's Leasing Division calculated that SLA needed to recover an amortised cost of $2,000 per month from the tenant, over the duration of the tenancy.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: The SLA's Leasing Division then asked the SLA's Valuer what the impact would be on the guide rent if the plot was enlarged, the additional land cleared and SLA recovered the amortised cost of the land clearance from the tenant as part of the monthly rental.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: The SLA's Valuer told CPIB in the interview that, in her view, the guide rent for the larger land area of 23,164 square metres, once cleared of vegetation, should be $26,500.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: But if the tenant paid the clearance costs, then the guide rent of $24,500 could be maintained.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: Throughout this episode, the SLA Valuer did not know the identity of the prospective tenant.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: The SLA Valuer only learnt that the tenant was Minister Shanmugam after the matter was reported in the media.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: The SLA Valuer also did not know the rental amount which the Leasing Division had negotiated with the tenant.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: The SLA's Leasing Division then added the amortised cost of $2,000 per month to what the Leasing Division treated as the guide rent of $24,500, calculated the minimum rental to be achieved at $26,500 and confirmed that the agreed rental of $26,500 met this threshold.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: Instead, SLA treated the guide rent as $24,500, but with the additional $2,000 amortised cost to also be recovered.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: CPIB has also confirmed that this lack of precision in the process of deriving the guide rent did not result from any ill intent on the part of any SLA officers involved.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: It found no evidence of any mala fide abuse of position in the valuation.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin and Ms Hazel Poa asked whether the terms of the lease agreements of these properties were standard as compared to other black and white bungalows managed by SLA.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: Mr Leong Mun Wai and Mr Leon Perera asked about the costs incurred in maintenance and upgrading works for these two properties.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: Tenancies are granted on two-year or three-year terms, and up to a maximum of 3+3+3 years in the first instance when entering into a tenancy agreement.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: In deciding on the length of the tenancy, SLA will take into account various factors, including the likely capital expenditure that the tenant will incur to live in the property.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: Under the terms of the tenancy agreement, all approved improvements undertaken by the tenant that remain usable, will subsequently become the property of the landlord and revert to state ownership upon return of the property.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: As such, tenants who incur substantial capital expenditure for improvement works will be granted longer tenure, to allow for the amortisation of their expenses over a longer period.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: Both the tenancy periods of 26 and 31 Ridout Road were within the maximum allowable tenancy of 3+3+3 years for residential properties rented out by SLA or SLA's MAs at any one time.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: This was also within the cap of 3+3+3 years tenancy that SLA can grant, at any one time.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: As the landlord, it is the role of SLA to ensure that the properties rented out are in a reasonably good condition so that tenants are able to reside in these properties safely.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: It shows the scope of the works done by SLA for 26 Ridout Road and 31 Ridout Road, compared to the works done for other SLA black and white state properties.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: The works included general building repairs, electrical rewiring, water pump repair, sewerage repair, horticulture works, road and fencing repairs, and treatment for termites.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: Members can get a sense of the nature and scope of the works done from the pictures at Handout 4.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: This comprised general building repairs, roof repair and waterproofing, electrical rewiring, replacing the water tank, horticultural works, road and fencing repairs, and treatment for termites.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: Members can get a sense of the nature and scope of the works done from the pictures at Handout 5.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: The works done by SLA for 26 and 31 Ridout Road were to make both properties safe and habitable.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: The scope of works is comparable to that for other SLA black and white properties, as Chart 3 shows.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: The valuation of the property will have factored in the condition of the property after works are done to bring them to a habitable condition.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: SLA did a cost-benefit analysis to confirm that the rent that can be received will more than justify the works over the expected service life of these works, which can be 10 years or more.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: And once rented out, the tenant is responsible for the proper maintenance of the property.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: CPIB's report also stated that "SLA policy is that upon expiry of the lease, the tenant is responsible for repairing any damage to the property, where appropriate.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: The property with any improvements approved by SLA will be surrendered to SLA as is, without any right of claims or recovery of costs by the tenant".

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: An additional piece of work relating to 26 Ridout Road was the clearance of the heavily vegetated land.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: An example where SLA also cleared land to address disamenities is at a state property in Dalvey Estate in 2019.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: SLA carried out partial site clearance even after the tenancy started, due to feedback from the surrounding neighbours and the tenant on mosquito breeding, which was not resolved despite repeated fogging.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: The two Ministers had requested the Prime Minister to carry out a review into the rentals of 26 and 31 Ridout Road.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: As I stated earlier, that the Prime Minister had directed CPIB to investigate the matter shows his determination to establish the facts of the case and to get to the bottom of the matter.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: The Review arrived at three key conclusions, drawing substantially from CPIB's independent report.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: First, CPIB found no evidence of corruption or criminal wrongdoing in the two rental transactions of the Ridout Road state properties by Ministers Shanmugam and Balakrishnan.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: CPIB found that the Direct Tenancy rules were applied fairly for both rental transactions.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: The investigation did not reveal any corrupt intent on the part of any person, or any inducement given to any individual involved in the processing of the rentals.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: CPIB found no preferential treatment given to the Ministers and their spouses, and no disclosure of privileged information in the process of the rental transactions.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: There was no evidence to suggest any abuse of position by the Ministers for personal gain.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: Second, both the Ministers and the public officers, as well as private sector intermediaries involved, conducted themselves properly in the two rental transactions.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: They were aware of their duty to declare and avoid any conflict of interest and took appropriate steps to prevent any potential or actual conflict of interest from arising.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: This is testimony to the integrity of our officers.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: I want to thank our officers for acting professionally and with integrity in carrying out their duties.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: I should add that the thorough investigations by CPIB proceeded smoothly because the persons interviewed, including Ministers and their spouses, public officers and private sector managing and property agents, were forthcoming and cooperative, allowing the investigations to proceed smoothly.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: The extensive questions posed by Members from both sides of the House reflect the importance we place on the integrity and quality of Singapore's system of Government.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: So, Mr Deputy Speaker, Sir, let us continue, generation after generation, to instil strong values in our people, especially the men and women in politics and public service, to continue serving with integrity and excellence, even when no one is looking.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: I will be ready to answer any clarifications that Members may seek after my colleagues have made their Statements.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: The Second Minister for Law, Minister for Foreign Affairs and the Minister for Law will be making related Ministerial Statements.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: I will allow Members to raise points of clarification on all four Statements after the Minister for Law's Statement.
